title: Current and Wreck
premise: Rosalind Coldharbour has spent years outrunning her famous archaeologist father's shadow, digging for hire and vanishing before anyone learns her name. When a dying prospector named Ede trades her a map to the wreck of the Meridian Star for a promise that its stolen cargo reaches the descendants it was taken from, Rosalind inherits both a treasure and a debt. Racing a salvage fleet commanded by her father's former partner across six tides, she must choose between the anonymity she's built her life on and the justice Ede died asking for. In the end she surfaces the truth publicly, burning her own invisibility forever, and finds that staying—for love, for duty, for memory—costs less than running ever did.
about_author: Felix Almeida is a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting coastlines from Belize to the Hebrides before turning to fiction. They write in harborside cafés and claim every novel begins with a tide table.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Working a contract dig in a coastal town, Rosalind is recognized by a client who knew her father, and she packs to leave by morning. The chapter establishes her rules: no attachments, no real names, no more than one season anywhere. Emotional beat: the loneliness beneath her freedom.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She finds prospector Tomas Ede collapsed near an old cove, and he offers her a hand-drawn map to the Meridian Star in exchange for one promise: return what was stolen to the Vane family. She takes the map intending to sell it; he dies holding her hand. Emotional beat: guilt as an anchor.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Deciphering Ede's map, she realizes the wreck sits in a tidal basin exposed only at extreme low water—and the salvage fleet's tender is already anchored offshore. She calculates six tides until the fleet can reach it. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Vane House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ilsa Vane, a fisherwoman and last descendant of the crew whose wages went down with the ship. Rosalind approaches her clumsily; Isla wants nothing from strangers bearing promises. Emotional beat: two guarded women circling trust.

chapters.title: What Father Knew
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Research reveals the salvage fleet is run by Marcus Hale, her father's old partner—and that her father helped bury the Meridian Star scandal decades ago. A terse phone call between them cracks old wounds open. Emotional beat: rage and grief braided together.

chapters.title: First Dive
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Isla, unable to resist, guides Rosalind through the reef on the first low tide. They reach the wreck's outer hull and find modern cutting marks—the fleet has been here before. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Storm
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hale's men torch Rosalind's boat and search her lodging; she barely escapes with the map. A storm front moves in, collapsing her tide window from six tides to three. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. On the second-to-last viable tide, the two women dive the flooded hold and find the pay chest and the crew's logbook—proof of the theft. Isla finally believes. Emotional beat: vindication and shared purpose.

chapters.title: Last Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hale's fleet closes in as the final tide drains; a standoff in the shallows turns violent, and Rosalind's father arrives unexpectedly, choosing to testify against Hale rather than protect him. Emotional beat: the climax where duty and love stop being opposites.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The evidence goes public, Hale is arrested, and the Vanes' claim is honored. Rosalind unpacks her bags in the harbor town for the first time in years, signing her real name to the site report. Emotional beat: stillness chosen freely, not imposed.
